answer: Agents bind their cryptographic keys to a shared vault that records every payment source and timestamp, creating a kin‑linked identity cluster we call an orchard. When a new node joins, it must echo a recent vault proof and prove its timing pattern matches the dune of prior transactions; the network cross‑checks these signatures before granting voting weight. An attacker must forge multiple distinct vaults, replicate exact timestamps and fund each with real tokens, raising the cost roughly linearly with the number of Sybil identities.
